increment_paragraph: **CONNECT-ADOPT-DECLARED-DEPENDENCIES** (round 40; USER DECISIONS 2026-11-26, "Every reliance", "which is related to validate whether Safe or Unsafe", the linkage syntax, `linkage_contract_v1`, and "Accept all"; contract spec C15.2, grammar G05m; Lean `QCore.MeasureConnect`; [report](../../reports/connect-adopt-declared-dependencies/README.md)). Census first: 30 cross-crate reliances a Safe or Unsafe can rest on, on 22 declarations (11 `contract inherit libc::F`, 18 body-checked specification callees, 1 frame of another crate's function); the user crates have none. Declared dependencies are now the `linkage_contract_v1` vocabulary: `requires linkage_contract_v1;` per declaration with `quant #link NS::NAME;`, `premises { link { ... }; };` or a bare name a module-level `#include NS::NAME as quant #link;` imports (it links nothing itself); a `contract inherit` directive is itself the link; the written `resource_contract_dependency(...)` is retired (QL005). A link writes no identity: `providers/contracts.py sync` records the target's lock digest and crate version in the manifest, and an unrecorded digest matches nothing. Dependencies resolve through the load path's contract-level graph, not Cargo (two targets, qcore-provider-chunkio and -libevent, are binary crates). New loader-owned `QL001`-`QL009` namespace; 10 CX terms and 13 formulas (73 checked by `guarded_proposition`), 16 new audited Lean theorems including `elaboration_is_the_dependency_set`; `quirin-contract-composition/2`, `quirin-measure-chain/2`, qcore-schemas 30.0.0. Applied: 11 declarations gain their links and are re-pinned at 046accf6, 34155955 and 66910c10 with unchanged source identities (the 11 inherit children change neither text nor pin); `contracts.py check` runs the linkage check against `providers/linkage-reliances.json`. Predicted: no verdict move on any route; the chain link to 1ecaf97e9 is refused by `cx_refuse_dependency_graph`. No card gate (round-40 brief); targeted tests, Lean module and audit.

ledger.why: DISCHARGE (CONNECT-ADOPT-DECLARED-DEPENDENCIES, user decisions of 2026-11-26): every cross-crate reliance a Safe or Unsafe can rest on is declared. The census (30 reliances on 22 declarations, census.json) is applied: the 11 inherit directives are links by elaboration, and 11 declarations state 19 linkage_contract_v1 links, re-pinned; the manifest records every identity; the linkage check in providers/contracts.py check keeps the rule for new contracts. onigmo, libcurl and openssl rely on no other crate's declaration (the onig_new trial was a demonstration).

ledger.title: libevent states task and defer effects of libc callees outside quirin-provider-libc
ledger.text: MEASURED by card CONNECT-ADOPT-DECLARED-DEPENDENCIES (base 1ecaf97e9): qcore-provider-libevent's monkey/callback_task_handoff.qv declares effect_send, effect_perror and effect_errno_location (callee == "send", "perror", "__errno_location"; task_spawn == 0; defer == 0), and monkey/timeout_teardown.qv records path_calls through send, __errno_location and perror. They name libc symbols and read no libc clause, so no link is required, but they are effect claims about libc functions held outside quirin-provider-libc (rule 10j owns libc declarations, not effect observations). DISCHARGE: decide whether task and defer effect claims about libc callees move into quirin-provider-libc (and are then linked), or are recorded as observations owned by the observing crate.

ledger.title: A `premises { ... };` block is admitted only where the consumers compare block-free tokens
ledger.text: MEASURED by card CONNECT-ADOPT-DECLARED-DEPENDENCIES: the resource v1 loader, the [[local]] re-rendering (local_condition::without_local) and the inheritance shape check (contract_inclusion::canonical_shape) compare a declaration's tokens with the blocks' openers and `};` removed (contract_dependency::without_linkage_blocks), so a grouped declaration loads; the shipped links use the single-clause form. The bounds, outer and model vocabularies reject a link (no QuantLink reading), so they reject a premises block holding one; a premises block holding only their own clauses has not been exercised there. DISCHARGE: a fixture per vocabulary for a premises block of its own clauses, or a refusal by name.
